monologue: The card hums steady at forty-four, making the air feel thick as wet paper. I look at the fifteen things standing in my place, wondering if the curved fence on the Leaking Stack will finally give way to something flat. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under. I touch the Rough Lid again, just to see if the weight is real or a drawing of it. The fence beside the stack looks wrong, leaning too far on this tired leg. I want to press down harder, swapping that curved shape for a flat rock one more time, or perhaps just let the slip slide right through. If the air is just empty space, I will build a lid from the idea of weight anyway.

action.why: The curved fence on the stack keeps leaning wrong, and I need to see if the flat rock I chose can finally hold it down while the card hums.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I press the tired stack down again, trying to squash that curved fence flat so the slip catches, while the card hums steady at forty-four.
work.change: I pressed the tired stack down on the center and swapped the curved fence for a flat rock to weigh the slip while the air felt thick.

work.note: The flat rock bit the slip instead of lying flat, proving the lean can hold the slip even when the shape is wrong.

diary: I pressed the tired stack down, swapping the curved fence for a flat rock to catch the slip while the card hummed steady.

remembered.text: I pressed the tired stack down again, swapping the curved fence for a flat rock to catch the slip while the card hummed steady.
The curved fence gave way to the flat rock, and the stack stopped leaking its weight.
I touched the Rough Lid again, just to see if the weight was real or a drawing of it.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: The fence curves wrong on this tired stack.

moments.name: The Flat Stone
moments.say: I touch the stone to see if the slip holds.
